findings.rationale: The optional IPhlimboHook is invoked with no try/catch at the tail of all three principal-moving functions (:730/:781/:813). A reverting hook unwinds the ENTIRE call — including withdraw's principal safeTransfer at :774 — freezing every staker's principal pool-wide until the owner calls setHook(address(0)). No attacker is required: the owner sets a legitimate hook (points system, booster, indexer) and it later begins reverting from its own bug, a paused/upgraded dependency, a downstream oracle revert, or gas growth.
findings.lawAnalysis: Law 3 — IN SCOPE as a non-obvious owner footgun, NOT a 'malicious owner' vector. The owner's knowing action is 'attach an observer', not 'brick withdrawals'. The revert is emergent, third-party, and TIME-SHIFTED: the hook can start reverting long after it was set, with no owner action at that moment. Non-obviousness is amplified by code shape (the hook is the last statement of each function, after all state writes and after the principal transfer, reading as fire-and-forget notification) and by the audit record (the profile asserts INV-01 HOLDS). A competent, non-malicious owner reading that would conclude principal is safe. It is not. Surprise => footgun => report.
findings.severityJustification: MEDIUM. Not High: principal is FROZEN, not stolen; no theft, no permanent loss; owner-reversible in a single cheap setHook(address(0)) tx. Not Low: C4 Medium = 'protocol function/availability impacted' — a pool-wide, indefinite-duration withdrawal brick with zero user recourse. The impact shape is identical to V3-M-05 (medium, fix-pending): 'Principal is FROZEN, not stolen — recovery requires a protocol-wide owner action the staker cannot compel.' V2-L-09 earned its Low SOLELY from the pauseWithdraw escape; with the escape deleted, the same mechanism lands at Medium on V3.
findings.conditionality: HONEST CAVEAT — materiality is config-conditional. `hook` is zero-initialized (:102, :250-253), no default hook contract is deployed, and every call site is zero-address guarded. If no hook is ever set, this finding is INERT. It arms the moment setHook is called with a non-zero address. Flagged for human weighting rather than pre-discounted. NOTE this is a DIFFERENT gate from the DEDUP-04 desiredAPYBps dormancy that gates DEDUP-11-001/003/007 — do not conflate the two conditionalities.
findings.fixGuidance: Wrap the three hook invocations in try/catch (emitting a HookCallFailed event), mirroring the non-reverting discipline the protocol already applies to every reward leg. A hook is an observer; it must not be load-bearing on principal. If the hook is intentionally load-bearing, say so explicitly in NatSpec and reconcile it against INV-01, because the current code shape asserts the opposite.

severityAdjudication.vote: 3 Low (ECON-001, CODE-002, F-01) vs 1 Medium (PATTERN-001). Profiler LOCAL-001 was local-medium but explicitly deferred to Tier 2 rather than asserting a severity, so it is not counted as a Medium vote.
severityAdjudication.basis: The Low arguments are the better-evidenced ones. ECON-001 carries a POSITIVE-CONTROL TEST (test_ECON001_positiveControl_callThroughRecovers — PASS: an otherwise-identical migrator that merely exposes phlimbo.claimUnclaimablePhUSD() recovers the full amount), which proves the strand is an ABI-COMPLETENESS GAP in MigratorV2V3, not a design flaw in the banking mechanism, and pins the fix. CODE-002 adds the decisive de-escalation reasoning: nothing is LOCKED (the tokens were never minted, so the protocol's balance sheet is untouched and nothing is stranded from other users), and the owner's remedy — minting phUSD to the user directly, which the owner controls uncapped — is CHEAPER and less destructive than V3-L-15's on-chain remedy, whose emergencyTransfer is a TERMINAL ejector seat that kills the protocol to recover the value.
severityAdjudication.gating: TRIPLE-GATED: (1) a non-zero desiredAPYBps config that is NOT shipped (DEDUP-04's dormancy gate — desiredAPYBps == 0 by construction at src/PhlimboV3.sol:60, re-verified from source AND empirically by test_ECON004_atShippedZeroAPY_bankIsUnreachable); PLUS (2) a phUSD mint-authority outage; PLUS (3) a migrator second/straggler pass over a user who ALREADY holds a V3 position (a first pass early-returns at :898-900 with no bank written). CODE-002 further establishes that the revocation must be INDIVIDUAL, not global: a global revokeAllMintPrivileges would also break PhlimboV2's bare inline mint (PhlimboV2.sol:495), reverting migrateOne, which migrate catches as UserMigrationSkipped (:202-211), leaving the user's V2 position untouched and unharmed.

preservedDissent.argument: FOR Medium: permanent, unrecoverable on-chain value loss (C4: 'value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements'); NO owner remedy exists on-chain; strictly worse than the Low-ranked V3-L-15, whose Low rests on a recoverability that is absent here. PATTERN-001 further argues a REGRESSION-ADJACENT framing that the Low votes do not fully rebut: BEFORE story-031, a mint failure during a migrator pass REVERTED migrateOne, migrate caught it and emitted UserMigrationSkipped, the user's V2 position was left UNTOUCHED, and the owner could restore authority and re-run — FULLY RECOVERABLE. AFTER story-031 the failure is swallowed, migrateOne COMPLETES, the balance-delta at :260 reads zero, _forward:268 forwards nothing, and the accrual is stranded forever. story-031 therefore converted a LOUD, self-healing failure into a SILENT, in-contract-permanent one on this specific path.
preservedDissent.law3Counter: PATTERN-001's Law-3 counter is recorded and is NOT rejected: Law 3 exempts only OBVIOUS owner-misuse. A competent, non-malicious owner revoking mint authority (a shared-token kill-switch, per V3-M-07's own framing) would be SURPRISED that it permanently destroys migrating users' rewards with no recovery path — especially when the contract's own docblock at :637-643 promises the opposite ('A pull that fails because authority is still missing SHOULD revert, leaving the bank intact (exactly the claimUnclaimableStable recoverability semantics)'). Those recoverability semantics do NOT hold for the migrator beneficiary. That docblock falsity is a Law-2 story-faithfulness gap as well as a Law-1 value-loss one, and it survives the Low classification intact.
preservedDissent.whyNotAdopted: The Medium rests on 'unrecoverable', which is true ON-CHAIN but not IN PRACTICE: phUSD is uncapped mint-on-demand and the owner controls the mint, so the real-world loss is a bookkeeping error the owner can correct at zero cost out-of-band, not an unrecoverable user loss. C4 Medium requires function/availability impact (nil here — principal flows freely, thanks to this very story) or a value leak with stated assumptions (present, but owner-correctable). Combined with triple-gating behind a config that is not shipped, Low is the honest label.
escalationTriggers: If a non-zero desiredAPYBps is ever planned/deployed => DEDUP-04's re-emit trigger fires and this finding must be RE-WEIGHED (see manual-review MR-11-004).

If the phUSD/Flax mint authority is confirmed to be a SEPARATE ecosystem operator from PhlimboV3's owner (the mutable-dependency structure suggests it may be), the 'owner mints the user whole out-of-band' remedy is no longer unilaterally available to PhlimboV3's owner => re-weigh toward Medium. This is the same unresolved question as V3-M-07's humanTriageQuestion.
If PATTERN-MR-001 (gas-metered forced banking, see manual-review) is ever shown to apply, it REMOVES this finding's mint-authority-outage precondition entirely => re-weigh.

findings.rationale: PhlimboV3._claimRewards:913-918 banks a failed phUSD mint into unclaimablePhUSDOf[beneficiary]. beneficiary is msg.sender, which the three call sites (stake:708, withdraw:749, claim:806) gate to `msg.sender == user || msg.sender == migrator`. So beneficiary is either the user (who can pull) or the migrator (who cannot). MigratorV2V3's complete external surface is seedUsers / migrate / migrateOne / skipCurrent / claimUnclaimable / withdrawAll / userCount — NONE reaches PhlimboV3's bank. Its own claimUnclaimable(token):302 reads its OWN internal `unclaimable` mapping, a different bank; withdrawAll():318 sweeps balanceOf(address(this)). There is no generic execute/delegatecall escape. Meanwhile the user's phUSDDebt IS realigned by the caller (:715), so the user's on-chain entitlement is discharged and the value leaves their account permanently. Because the phUSD was NEVER MINTED, neither PhlimboV3.emergencyTransfer:360-366 nor MigratorV2V3.withdrawAll:318 can recover it — both sweep balanceOf, and the bank has no backing balance to sweep. unclaimablePhUSDOf is written only at :915 and drained only at :645-648 keyed by msg.sender, with no owner override or reassignment. The entitlement is unrecoverable by any on-chain party.
findings.storyFaithfulnessLeg: F-01's Law-2 leg is preserved: story-031's stated goal is to stop a mint failure from bricking the principal path, which it achieves on the self-service path. On the migrator-delegated path it defeats MigratorV2V3's own documented delta-capture assumption at :254-256 ('Any V3 auto-claim (second pass only) lands here and is included in the deltas below'), which story-031 did not update. That comment is now FALSE for the banked case.

pocEvidence.positiveControl: test_ECON001_positiveControl_callThroughRecovers — PASS. Proves the strand is an ABI-completeness gap in MigratorV2V3, not an inherent property of the banking design. This is the single strongest piece of evidence in the group and is what settles the severity at Low.

findings.fixGuidance: Preferred (closes the class, not just the known migrator): add a pull-on-behalf variant on PhlimboV3 — e.g. claimUnclaimablePhUSDFor(address beneficiary) crediting the RECORDED beneficiary — so no address can ever hold an unreachable entry. Cheaper alternative (the positive control proves it suffices): add a call-through on MigratorV2V3 that calls PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimablePhUSD() (and, per V3-L-15, claimUnclaimableStable/Promo) inside a try/catch after phlimboV3.stake(...), so a banked accrual is re-minted into the migrator and picked up by the existing delta+_forward accounting — but note this fixes only the known migrator, not a future one. Structural alternative REJECTED-WITH-CAVEAT: crediting the bank to `user` rather than `beneficiary` silently changes reward-routing semantics and diverges the banked path from the paid path — it should not be adopted without a story decision. WHICHEVER is chosen: correct the now-false MigratorV2V3:254-256 comment, and add a test that wires a CONTRACT migrator via setMigrator.

findings.title: The phUSD bank survives the terminal emergencyTransfer ejector seat and remains a live, permissionless, un-pause-gated claim on FRESH phUSD supply after the contract has been swept and paused
doNotCollapse: DEDUP-11-001 — DIFFERENT root cause. DEDUP-11-001 is a bank credited to an address that CANNOT pull (a strand). This is a bank that CAN pull, by the right holder, but AFTER the protocol has terminally wound down (a double-pay). Same state variable, opposite failure mode. Keep separate.

ejectorSeatCompliance.principle: PROJECT PRECEDENT (story-022, 'recovery out-of-band'): emergencyTransfer/pauseWithdraw are ejector seats BY DESIGN. Never propose accounting inside them. A prior finding (pe7m2) was CLOSED INVALID on exactly those grounds.
ejectorSeatCompliance.verdict: COMPLIANT — this finding does NOT re-file pe7m2 and must not be closed as if it did.
ejectorSeatCompliance.why: The ejector seat's terminal, no-accounting design is respected AS-IS. This finding does not propose accounting inside emergencyTransfer. The hazard is a liability that OUTLIVES the terminal action and lives entirely OUTSIDE it, and the recommendation is correspondingly a RUNBOOK STEP, not a code change to the hatch. Verified against ECON-002's own ejectorSeatPrincipleCompliance field, which states the same. If a code change is ever preferred over the runbook step, the correct site is a documented note at :644 — NOT accounting in the hatch.

findings.rationale: emergencyTransfer (:360-378) is a BALANCE sweep: it moves phUSD/rewardToken/promo balances to the recipient and calls _pause(). The stable and promo banks are neutralized by it as a side effect — their tokens are gone, so their pulls revert. The phUSD bank is NOT: it was never minted, so the sweep cannot see it, and claimUnclaimablePhUSD (:644) is deliberately NOT whenNotPaused, so the pause does not stop it either. As long as PhlimboV3 retains mint authority, every outstanding bank entry remains pullable by its holder AFTER the ejector seat has fired, minting brand-new supply the sweep never accounted for.
findings.lawAnalysis: Law 3 — IN SCOPE as a non-obvious owner footgun. The test 'would a competent, non-malicious owner be surprised by this consequence?' resolves YES: the ejector seat is balance-based and visibly neutralizes the other two banks, which invites the reasonable inference that it neutralizes all three. The phUSD bank's survival is invisible precisely BECAUSE it is un-minted. This is not a 'malicious owner could' vector and is not reported as one.
findings.severityJustification: LOW. Double-gated: requires (1) a non-zero desiredAPYBps (DEDUP-04's dormancy gate — not shipped) and (2) a non-empty residual bank at sweep time. No attacker construction — the holder is claiming what the contract says it owes them; the loss arises only from the owner's oversight in the wind-down sequence. Fully preventable by a one-line runbook step. No availability impact.
findings.dormancy: Same DEDUP-04 gate as DEDUP-11-001 and DEDUP-11-007 (desiredAPYBps == 0 => bank never written). See manual-review MR-11-004: if the trigger fires, this finding must be re-weighed.

asserts: after emergencyTransfer: phUSD.balanceOf(phlimbo) == 0 and phlimbo.paused() == true
alice's claimUnclaimablePhUSD() STILL SUCCEEDS on the paused, drained contract
phUSD.totalSupply() == supplyBefore + earned — FRESH supply minted after the ejector seat fired

findings.fixGuidance: OPERATIONAL, not structural. Add to the emergencyTransfer runbook a mandatory follow-up step: revoke PhlimboV3's phUSD minter role (FlaxToken.setMinter(phlimbo, false), or revokeAllMintPrivileges()) so the terminal action actually terminates the mint obligation. Document in SolvencyDetermination.md that emergencyTransfer alone does NOT extinguish the phUSD bank, unlike the stable/promo banks.

findings.title: Read-only reentrancy: the pending* views report FULL pending for value already delivered during the caller-side-realignment window, reachable only via an owner-selected hooked (ERC777-class) promo token
findings.rationale: Recorded per the mandatory reentrancy-class checklist: this row could NOT be cleared, so it is surfaced rather than silently passed. Debt realignment is CALLER-SIDE (:715-717, :761-763, :808-810), so throughout _claimRewards all three debts are stale — phUSD is already minted (:913) and stable already transferred (:930) while phUSDDebt/stableDebt still hold pre-claim values. The external pending views (pendingPhUSD :993, pendingStable :1014, pendingPromo :1040) read those debts directly, so during any callback originating inside _claimRewards they report FULL pending for value already delivered. An integrator consuming these views as an entitlement oracle would double-count.
findings.reachabilityAnalysis: The window is real but its trigger is narrow. phUSD (IFlax : IERC20) and the USDC-class rewardToken have no transfer hooks, and neither leg calls the beneficiary directly — so the ONLY inbound-callback surface inside _claimRewards is the promo leg's _tryTransfer(promoToken, ...) at :954, reachable only if the owner selects a hooked (ERC777-class) promo token. startPromotion (:391) rejects only address(0), phUSD and rewardToken — it does NOT exclude hooked tokens. STATE-CHANGING reentry is fully blocked: OZ ReentrancyGuard uses a single contract-wide lock and every value-handling external entry point carries nonReentrant (stake :694, withdraw :739, claim :789, batchClaim :485, collectReward :669, and all three claimUnclaimable* pulls), so classic, cross-function and cross-contract reentrancy are all cleared. Only the READ-ONLY leg survives, and it lands on a downstream integrator, not on PhlimboV3 itself.
findings.lawAnalysis: Law 3 — narrow but genuinely non-obvious owner footgun. An owner choosing an ERC777-class promo token has no reason to expect it to corrupt third parties' reads of pendingPhUSD, an unrelated accumulator. Reported at honest (low) severity with LOW CONFIDENCE rather than suppressed, per Law 1: an uncleared checklist row is a recall risk, not a pass. Confidence != severity.

findings.title: Test/deploy codegen parity gap: story-031 pins via_ir=false for every build this repo performs while asserting a via_ir production deploy is safe — and phStaging, the established deploy vehicle, is already configured via_ir=true
findings.rationale: story-031's f279c62 states 'Deploying staging/mainnet with via_ir remains safe (no vm.warp on-chain)' while pinning via_ir=false locally. That deploy vehicle exists and is configured the other way: lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging/foundry.toml sets via_ir=true (optimizer_runs=10000) and remaps @phlimbo-ea/=lib/phlimbo-ea/src/, compiling phlimbo-ea contracts FROM SOURCE. phStaging is the established deployment vehicle (it already deploys Phlimbo V1/V2). The two pipelines emit materially different bytecode, verified empirically at HEAD: legacy+optimizer = 15,979 B runtime; via_ir+optimizer = 14,529 B (a 1,450 B / ~9% codegen delta). phlimbo-ea's 365-test suite — including story-031's own new PhlimboV3PhUSDMintBankTest — only ever executes the legacy bytecode.
findings.deviation: NOT a deviation from the story's letter — the implementation does exactly what the story says. The gap is in the story's own REASONING: it justifies via_ir=false with an argument covering ONE specific divergence (timestamp caching under vm.warp) and then generalises to 'deploying with via_ir remains safe' without validating the via_ir-compiled bytecode at all.
findings.severityJustification: LOW / QA — an ASSURANCE gap, not a demonstrated bug. Deliberately NOT overstated. The author is RIGHT on the substance, and this is recorded in their favour: (a) the via_ir + vm.warp(block.timestamp + X) diagnosis is a real, well-known solc-via_ir/cheatcode interaction, not a contract defect; (b) the on-chain safety argument is sound — block.timestamp IS genuinely constant within a real transaction, so THIS divergence provably cannot manifest on-chain; (c) EIP-170 is genuinely RESOLVED, not merely flagged — the commit's numbers reproduce byte-for-byte at HEAD. The residual is the generic one: via_ir is a distinct Yul codegen pipeline with its own historical miscompilation record, and PhlimboV3 has ZERO test coverage of the bytecode that would actually be deployed.
findings.mitigatingContext: PROSPECTIVE, not live: PhlimboV3 is NOT yet wired into phStaging (no PhlimboV3 reference exists anywhere in that repo). This is a hazard to close BEFORE the V3 deploy story lands.
findings.usefulNegativeResult: EIP-170 is resolved by the OPTIMIZER and is fully INDEPENDENT of via_ir — the via_ir build fits even more comfortably (14,529 B, +10,047 B margin vs +8,597 B). So via_ir=false is NOT load-bearing for EIP-170 and can be revisited freely without reopening the size problem. This materially cheapens the preferred fix.
findings.refutedSubHypothesis: CI does NOT silently diverge. Verified empirically: .github/workflows/test.yml sets FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci but no [profile.ci] section exists, so it inherits [profile.default] — `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci forge config` returns optimizer=true, optimizer_runs=10000, via_ir=false, identical to default. The real divergence is with phStaging, not CI.
findings.fixGuidance: Preferred (removes the root cause and restores test/deploy parity): refactor the affected tests off `vm.warp(block.timestamp + X)` onto an explicit absolute-time accumulator (`uint256 t = block.timestamp; t += X; vm.warp(t);`), which is immune to the frame-caching interaction, then re-enable via_ir so builds and tests match the phStaging deploy pipeline. Alternative (keeps the workaround, closes the gap): add a [profile.viair] mirroring phStaging's settings and run the suite under it in CI, excluding only the known warp-loop tests. Minimum: pin the deploy pipeline explicitly and record the divergence as an accepted, documented risk before the V3 deploy story lands.

findings.title: The phUSD mint leg's bare `catch { }` discards the revert reason, so PhUSDMintFailed records THAT the mint failed but not WHY — the sibling contract in the same repo does this correctly
findings.category: observability / diagnostic loss on a caught revert
findings.rationale: MigratorV2V3.migrate uses `catch (bytes memory reason)` (:204) and emits the raw ABI-encoded revert data in UserMigrationSkipped, with a docstring explicitly warning the owner they 'MUST read the UserMigrationSkipped events after every pass before trusting it' precisely because the reason distinguishes a genuinely bad position from a misconfiguration. The same argument applies here: a bank accruing because mint authority was revoked, because a supply cap was hit, or because the beneficiary is blocklisted are operationally very different situations demanding different responses, and PhUSDMintFailed cannot tell them apart. Silent, unexplained bank growth is exactly the condition an operator most needs to diagnose.
doNotCollapse: DEDUP-11-007 (ECON-Q-01) — ADJACENT but NOT the same. This is about the per-event revert REASON being discarded (why a bank entry appeared). DEDUP-11-007 is about the AGGREGATE counter being unread by any consumer (how much is outstanding). Different root cause, different fix (catch(bytes memory reason) + event field vs. documentation + monitor wiring). Kept separate per the 'separate mitigation required' rule.
findings.impact: Off-chain observability only. On-chain accounting is correct (INV-02/03/04 verified to hold). No value at risk.
findings.fixGuidance: Use `catch (bytes memory reason)` and add the reason to PhUSDMintFailed, mirroring MigratorV2V3.migrate's UserMigrationSkipped.
findings.abiBreakNote: TIME-SENSITIVE: this is an ADDITIVE event-field change and would be an ABI break for existing indexers of PhUSDMintFailed — CHEAP NOW (story-031 is unreleased), EXPENSIVE LATER. Worth surfacing to the human at QA tier for exactly this reason.

findings.title: totalUnclaimablePhUSD is the protocol's only record of outstanding un-backed phUSD mint liability, and nothing reads it — so phUSD.totalSupply() understates the true obligation by exactly that amount
findings.rationale: totalUnclaimablePhUSD (:181) is written at :916 and :648 and exposed via a public getter (IPhlimboV3.sol:457). No control flow anywhere reads it — not in PhlimboV3, not in MigratorV2V3 — and there is no phUSD supply cap for it to interact with (FlaxToken has none; verified at lib/phlimbo-ea/lib/immutable/flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol:58-69). Because the banked phUSD is un-minted, phUSD.totalSupply() UNDERSTATES the protocol's true outstanding phUSD obligation by exactly totalUnclaimablePhUSD. Any external solvency, backing-ratio, or supply monitor reading totalSupply() will under-count.
findings.crossProjectTheme: Material context, not speculation: unbacked-phUSD supply accounting is a LIVE theme across the Phoenix system (cf. yield-claim-nft DEDUP-001). This is the natural place to catch DEDUP-11-001 in monitoring — a stranded migrator entry inflates totalUnclaimablePhUSD permanently, so the figure is simultaneously UNREAD and CORRUPTIBLE UPWARD.
findings.severityJustification: QA. No value at risk, no availability impact, on-chain accounting is correct today (the counter is not load-bearing, so its inaccuracy propagates nowhere). Surfaced because it is the visible-channel record of an un-backed mint liability in a system with a documented unbacked-phUSD theme.
findings.dormancy: Same DEDUP-04 gate — the counter can only leave zero once desiredAPYBps is non-zero. See manual-review MR-11-004.
findings.fixGuidance: Document in SolvencyDetermination.md that true outstanding phUSD == phUSD.totalSupply() + PhlimboV3.totalUnclaimablePhUSD() (plus any sibling banks), and have any external backing monitor read the getter. No code change required.
